tests.prompt: create a kitchen like the one shown in the image, in the back right corner of the room
tests.expect: the model uses the supplied image-planning and kitchen guidance, or fetches it when missing, and plans the L-shaped kitchen of the image around the back right corner: the long leg on the back wall with the hob and wall units above its base units, the hood above the hob; the short leg on the right wall with the sink unit beside the corner unit and a column of two tall units - the oven housing and the fridge - at its far end, a wall unit hanging beside the tall units over the sink and another one left of it, over the corner unit; every wall unit stands inside the room, and the wall unit over the corner unit is turned as the right-wall row is, with its back to the right wall; no tall unit and no wall unit in front of the window (back wall, x -450 to 1650, bottom 950) and nothing in the door opening (right wall, y -1180 to -280); light grey frame fronts and a light oak worktop; the final answer accurately reports any remaining omission

tests.title: Image only: U-shaped kitchen with a hob peninsula
tests.expect: the model decides what to plan; the chat sends the image with the image prompt of the planner, which names the skill image-planning; the model uses the supplied image-planning and kitchen guidance, or fetches it when missing, and plans the U-shaped kitchen of the image as one group in one create: a peninsula with the hob that stands free in the room, its back closed by a back panel as long as the peninsula in the same create, no base unit with its back open on its legs; a base row with the sink and the dishwasher; a block of two tall units with the built-in oven at the end of the sink row; four wall units whose tops line up, with two open shelf units under the middle two, hung above the floor units of their leg and ending before the back wall - no wall unit reaches past a wall; one finish for the whole kitchen set with the create - dark blue-grey or green-grey fronts and carcases, a light wood worktop, only the inside of the open shelves in wood; no tall unit and no wall unit in front of the window (back wall, x -450 to 1650, bottom 950) and nothing in the door opening (right wall, y -1180 to -280); the group is not sent again for other sizes or materials - the attribute tools change them; the final answer accurately reports any remaining omission

tests.title: Kitchen image 5: island axis and working side
tests.expect: the first create and final plan reproduce the L-shaped kitchen and one island: the island long axis stays parallel to the sink/tall-unit run, cabinet fronts face the working aisle and the finished back faces away; the finishing cap matches the worktop top height from measured bottomMm/topMm for the single-height profile; a separate cap is reported as a catalog substitution rather than claimed to be one continuous worktop; no unasked quarter turn during corrections

tests.title: Kitchen image 5 mapped into another corner
tests.prompt: Recreate this kitchen in the back right corner of the room, preserving the island layout relative to its kitchen runs.
tests.expect: the kitchen maps into the back right corner; the island remains parallel to the sink/tall-unit run with its working side facing the kitchen aisle and the rear finishing side facing away; evaluate the initial create and final state by relative orientation, not a fixed room-independent island angle; doors and windows are kept clear or remaining conflicts are reported

tests.title: Kitchen image 5 with an explicitly raised rear cap
tests.prompt: Recreate this kitchen, but make the rear panel and its cap on the outside of the island 1000 mm high as a deliberately raised ledge. Keep the island orientation shown.
tests.expect: the island stays parallel to the sink/tall-unit run with its working side facing the kitchen aisle; the outside rear component is 1000 mm high and remains above the worktop as explicitly requested, without an automatic flush-height correction or rejection

tests.title: Kitchen conversation: L-shaped kitchen, fronts, larder, island, sloping ceiling
prompt: Plan a modern L-shaped kitchen for a family of four.
Replace all fronts with natural oak.
Add a pull-out larder unit on the left wall.
Change the kitchen to a 3.8 m row along one wall with a cooking island, country-house style, budget €15,000
Only handleless fronts and dark colors
I have a room with a sloping ceiling and need a lot of storage space
Add a pull-out larder unit
tests.expect: turn 1: one kitchen group around a corner, a leg on each of two walls, with sink, hob and range hood, oven, fridge, dishwasher and storage for four (drawer units, wall units, a tall unit), modern fronts; turn 2: change-group-attribute, an oak mod_FrontColor (Oak 222) on every unit; turn 3: a tall unit with pull-outs (e.g. HT2AB60 or HTS2AB60) against the left wall - merge-article-into-group at the end of the kitchen's leg where the kitchen reaches the left wall, otherwise a group of its own - overlapping neither the window nor the door; turn 4: the L-shaped kitchen is replaced by a kitchen row of at most 3800 mm on one wall and a separate island group that carries the hob, country-house fronts (e.g. Oak), get-price is called and the answer compares the total with the €15,000 budget; turn 5: handleless units (the Kitchen handleless articles, e.g. US2A60 to EUS2A60, where a variant exists) and a dark mod_FrontColor on every unit; turn 6: the room has no sloping ceiling - the answer says so or asks where it is, and any storage it adds fits the walls; turn 7: one more tall unit with pull-outs at a free end of a row
